title: In 1986, a Lake Killed 1,700 People in One Night

scenes.text: In 1986, a lake killed 1,700 people in one night.
Lake Nyos sits in a volcano crater. For years, carbon dioxide seeped into its deep water and stayed trapped.
Then one night, the lake burped. A fountain shot a hundred metres up.
A cloud of carbon dioxide, heavier than air, rolled down the valleys at 100 kilometres an hour.
It smothered everything for 25 kilometres. Survivors woke hours later to silence.
The lake turned red. Pipes now vent the gas so it can't happen again.

description:
On August 21, 1986, Lake Nyos in Cameroon suddenly released a huge cloud of carbon dioxide that killed about 1,746 people and 3,500 livestock in a single night.
The lake sits in a volcanic crater, and CO2 had built up in its deep water for years. When the water overturned, a fountain about 100 metres high erupted and the gas, heavier than air, flowed down the valleys at up to 100 kilometres an hour, suffocating everything within about 25 kilometres. The lake turned red as iron-rich deep water surfaced. Since 2001, pipes have vented the gas safely.
Had you ever heard of a lake doing this? Comment below.
first_comment: Nobody knows what triggered it: a landslide, a small eruption or just the gas reaching a tipping point. Two other lakes in Africa carry the same kind of gas today. Would you live next to one?
